passage:
A museum guide named Alex could explain history clearly, but children often became bored during his tours. He used many dates and names, and the children forgot them quickly.
One day, a child asked, "Did people in the past have pets"
Alex stopped. He had never included that in his tour. He began telling stories about ancient cats, horses, and birds. The children listened closely.
After that, Alex changed his tours. He still gave important facts, but he connected them to daily life: food, games, clothes, animals, and family.
Visitors enjoyed the tours more.
Alex learned that facts are like doors. People enter more easily when the door connects to something they already care about.
